title: Every step you take, every call you make: the reliable agent stack — Giselle van Dongen, Restate
talk_summary: Giselle van Dongen presents Restate, an open-source durable-execution server that sits in front of agent services, journals every step (LLM calls, tool calls, timers, human approvals) and replays that journal to recover crashed or long-running agent runs exactly where they failed. She demos a Slack deep-research agent with planner/sub-agent/writer steps, human approval via durable promises, virtual-object sessions with per-key serialization, and signal/cancel primitives for steering a running agent loop.

takeaways.technique: Durable execution journal for long agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap each side-effecting step (LLM call, web search, tool call) in a durable step that emits an event to a journal server; on crash, replay the journal and resume at the failed step instead of restarting the whole run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by doing these durable steps if this fails somewhere here two hours or two months later it will recover to exactly that point

takeaways.technique: Durable promise / suspend for human approval
takeaways.what_they_do: Model human-in-the-loop gates as a durable promise that suspends the workflow (no compute while waiting) and unblocks when the human responds, surviving restarts and redeploys over weeks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we create a durable promise which lives in that journal a bit like a suspension point ... while we are waiting this process actually suspends

takeaways.what_they_do: Key agent sessions by ID (e.g. Slack thread) into a stateful actor with isolated key-value state; guarantee only one execution runs per key at a time, queueing the next behind it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this will guarantee that only one execution is running at a time. So a second execution will be cued behind the current one

takeaways.technique: Signal vs cancel to steer a running agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose execution IDs so other processes can inject state (signal) into a running loop or cancel it; a classifier LLM decides whether new input is relevant (signal) or warrants cancel-and-restart.
takeaways.evidence_quote: inject this via a signal if it's not really relevant ... then cancel what you're currently doing and start over again

takeaways.technique: Centralized LLM gateway handler with per-department flow control
takeaways.what_they_do: Pull inline LLM calls out into a dedicated durable gateway handler that does policy checks then the call; other agents call it via the service fabric, and concurrency limits can be set per caller (e.g. 300 concurrent calls per department).
takeaways.evidence_quote: one department is only allowed to run 300 calls to this LLM gateway at the same time

takeaways.technique: Push-based invocation for low-latency durable workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of workers pulling tasks from an orchestrator, the server pushes invocations to services, cutting latency and fitting serverless wake-up models; single binary, HA by running multiple instances snapshotting to object storage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: restate actually pushes the invocations and the benefit you get from that is that it has a much lower latency
